git.branches.checkedOut: {where, select, agent {Checked out in {agent}'s worktree: a branch is in one folder at a time.} other {Checked out in another worktree: a branch is in one folder at a time.}}
git.branches.heading: Branches
git.branches.noCommits: No commits yet, and agents' worktrees need one.
git.branches.stateBanner: Git is {state, select, merge {merging} rebase {rebasing} cherrypick {cherry-picking} revert {reverting} other {bisecting}} in the project folder. Finish or abort it in a terminal (or ask an agent to): Hive doesn't.
git.branches.trackLocal: A local {branch} tracking {remote}, and switch to it
git.branches.tracksNothing: tracks no remote branch: Push sets one
git.busy.agent: {agent} {status, select, starting {is starting} working {is working} waiting {is waiting for your answer} background {is waiting on background tasks it started} watching {is waiting for cards to change (a card watch)} other {stopped in the middle of a task when its sign-in expired}} in the project folder: {action, select, switch {switch branches} create {create and switch to a branch} other {pull}} once it has finished.
git.busy.slotHeld: {agent} holds the merge slot for {branch}: {action, select, switch {switch branches} create {create and switch to a branch} other {pull}} once that merge is done.
git.busy.slotWaiting: {agents} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} waiting for the merge slot for {branch}: {action, select, switch {switch branches} create {create and switch to a branch} other {pull}} once those merges are done.
git.busy.yourMerge: Your merge into {branch} is running: {action, select, switch {switch branches} create {create and switch to a branch} other {pull}} once it is done.
git.fetch.at: As of the last fetch, {when}. Hive never fetches by itself.
git.fetch.never: Never fetched. Hive never fetches by itself.
git.fetch.tip: Fetch every remote: ahead/behind and remote branches as they are now
git.history.heading: History
git.hiveVcs.dismiss: Don't show this here again (Project Settings still says so)
git.hiveVcs.more: … and {count, plural, one {# more} other {# more}}
git.hiveVcs.noVcs: No git repository holds this project; if you make one, Hive excludes .hive there by itself. With another version control system, add .hive to its ignore list.
git.hiveVcs.notExcluded: Hive adds it to the git repository's .git/info/exclude, but git doesn't ignore it: Hive couldn't write that file, or a .gitignore rule brings .hive back.
git.hiveVcs.otherVcs: This project is in a {vcs} working copy, which Hive doesn't set up: add .hive to its ignore list.
git.hiveVcs.synced: {service} copies the project folder, .hive included: exclude .hive in {service} if it lets you, or keep the project in a folder it doesn't sync.
git.hiveVcs.trackedDetail: Excluding .hive keeps new files out of git, but {count, plural, one {this one was committed before, so git still tracks it and commits its changes} other {these were committed before, so git still tracks them and commits their changes}}. Run `git rm -r --cached .hive` in the project folder, then commit: the files stay on disk.{notExcluded, select, yes { Hive couldn't exclude .hive either: a rule in a .gitignore may bring it back.} other {}}
git.hiveVcs.trackedTitle: {count, plural, one {# file in .hive is committed to git} other {# files in .hive are committed to git}}
git.hiveVcs.untrackMessage: {count, plural, one {Hive runs git rm --cached on it in {project}, and nothing else: git stops tracking it and stages its removal from the repository. The file stays on disk. Commit afterwards to finish.} other {Hive runs git rm --cached on them in {project}, and nothing else: git stops tracking them and stages their removal from the repository. The files stay on disk. Commit afterwards to finish.}}
git.hiveVcs.untrackTitle: {count, plural, one {Untrack this file?} other {Untrack these # files?}}
git.hiveVcs.untrackedDetail: Commit the change to finish (git commit). The files are still on disk.
git.hiveVcs.why: It holds this computer's sessions, transcript backups and launch settings, which don't belong in commits or shared copies.
git.identity.about: {hasGlobal, select, yes {Who {project}'s commits are made as, agents' too (git config --local). Leave both empty to use your global identity ({global}). On GitHub, its no-reply address keeps your email private.} other {Who {project}'s commits are made as, agents' too (git config --local). Leave both empty to use your global identity. On GitHub, its no-reply address keeps your email private.}}
git.identity.heading: Commit identity
git.identity.missing: Git has no {missing, select, both {user.name or user.email} name {user.name} other {user.email}} for this repository, so commits fail. Set them here (or in your global git config).
git.identity.name: Name
git.identity.public: Commits pushed to GitHub show {email} to anyone who reads them. GitHub's no-reply address (…@users.noreply.github.com, in GitHub's email settings) keeps your address private.
git.identity.title: Commit identity for this repository
git.init.conditional: Your git config has conditional includes (includeIf), which may set the {missing, select, both {name and email} name {name} other {email}} for this repository. Hive uses what you enter only where they don't, and saves it to this repository's config only, never your global one.
git.init.enterEmail: Enter the email your commits are made as
git.init.enterName: Enter the name your commits are made as
git.init.makes: Makes {name} a git repository on a branch called main, keeps its .hive out of git, and commits {empty, select, yes {nothing yet (an empty first commit)} other {everything in the folder}} as the first commit, so agents can work in worktrees at once.
git.init.nested: It is inside the git repository in {folder}: a repository inside another is usually a mistake, and that one will no longer see the files here as its own.
git.init.nestedAnyway: Make a repository of its own inside {folder} anyway
git.init.noIdentity: Git has no {missing, select, both {name or email} name {name} other {email}} to commit as: Hive saves what you enter to this repository's config only, never your global one.
git.init.noReply: On GitHub, its no-reply address keeps your email private.
git.init.resume: {name} is a git repository with no commits yet, and worktrees need one. This keeps its .hive out of git and commits {empty, select, yes {nothing yet (an empty first commit)} other {everything in the folder}} as the first commit.{gitignore, select, yes { Its own .gitignore is kept.} other {}}
git.init.title: Initialise {project} as a git repository
git.newBranch.blocked: It can't be switched to now: {why}

git.newBranch.title: New branch
git.parentRepo: This project is inside the git repository in {folder}, so the Git view only shows it: Hive changes only a project's own repository.
git.problem.cantRead: {problem}, so Hive can't read this repository.
git.pull.detached: HEAD is detached: switch to a branch to pull.
git.pull.noUpstream: {branch} tracks no remote branch to pull from.
git.pull.state: Git is {state, select, merge {merging} rebase {rebasing} cherrypick {cherry-picking} revert {reverting} other {bisecting}}: finish or abort it first.
git.pull.tip: Fetch {upstream} and bring {branch} up to it (only when that needs no merge)
git.push.detached: HEAD is detached: switch to a branch to push.
git.push.message: {branch} tracks no remote branch yet. Push it, and track it from now on:
git.push.noRemote: Add a remote to push to.
git.push.tipTrack: Push {branch} to a remote and track it
git.push.title: Push {branch}
git.remotes.addAbout: A repository to fetch from and push to: a URL (https://github.com/you/repo.git, git@github.com:you/repo.git) or a folder.
git.remotes.heading: Remotes
git.remotes.name: Name
git.remotes.none: No remotes: this repository is only on this computer. Add one (a GitHub repository's URL, say) to push to it.
git.setup.howTo: To use them, make it a repository: Initialise makes it one on a branch called main, keeps its .hive out of git, and commits its files, so agents can work in worktrees at once. Then add a remote under Branches & remotes to push it.
git.setup.withoutGit: Without git, agents work in the project folder, and Hive has no worktrees, merging or Git view for it.
git.state: {state, select, merge {merging} rebase {rebasing} cherrypick {cherry-picking} revert {reverting} other {bisecting}}
git.statusBar.tip: Git branch of the selected project
git.switch.idle: {agents} {count, plural, one {has a session in the project folder: it finds {branch} on the next turn.} other {have sessions in the project folder: they find {branch} on the next turn.}}
git.switch.message: The project folder leaves {current} for {branch}. Uncommitted changes come along when they don't clash with {branch}; if they do, git refuses and nothing changes.
git.switch.title: Switch {project} to {branch}?
git.tags.about: {onBranch, select, yes {Tags the commit the project folder has checked out ({branch}). With a message, it's an annotated tag.} other {Tags the commit the project folder has checked out. With a message, it's an annotated tag.}}
git.tags.heading: Tags
git.tags.name: Name
git.tags.none: No tags. Create tag… tags the commit the project folder has checked out.
git.tags.title: Tag {commit}
git.tip.fetched: As of the last fetch, {when}. Hive never fetches by itself.
git.tip.gone: It tracked {upstream}, which is gone from the remote.
git.tip.neverFetched: Never fetched: Hive never fetches by itself.
git.tip.noTracking: It tracks no remote branch: Push sets one.
git.tip.state: Git is {state, select, merge {merging} rebase {rebasing} cherrypick {cherry-picking} revert {reverting} other {bisecting}}: finish or abort it in a terminal.

git.tool.fixMissing: Install Git for Windows ({min} or later), or add the folder holding git.exe to your PATH, then Check again in Agent Setup (no need to restart Hive).
git.tool.fixOld: Update Git for Windows to {min} or later, then Check again in Agent Setup.
git.tool.missing: Git isn't installed (or isn't on Hive's PATH)
git.tool.oldLoses: {lost, select, recent {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts.} older {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts; moving a workspace can't repair its worktrees.} other {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts; Remove All and loading a template keep the branches of the worktrees they remove; moving a workspace can't repair its worktrees.}}
git.tool.tooOld: Git {version} is too old for Hive (it needs {min} or later)
git.tool.tooOldToRun: Hive's git commands fail with Git {version}: worktrees, merging, the Git tab and the unmerged counts don't work.
git.validate.nameLine: A name is one line, without < or >
git.validate.notUrl: That isn't a URL or path
git.validate.wholeUrl: Type the whole URL: its password or token is hidden here
